🇲🇽🚆 <u>MEXICO'S NEW PASSENGER TRAINS ARE DRIVING THE CONSTRUCTION RECOVERY: +7.5% IN MAY</u>

Construction production value grew 2.7% monthly and 7.5% annually in May, INEGI reported — eight straight months of growth and the strongest reading since August 2023. Transport and urbanization works jumped 9.3%, powered by the Mexico–Querétaro, Pachuca, Nogales and Nuevo Laredo passenger trains, with Tren Maya cargo still under construction, El Economista reports.

Public infrastructure is pulling the sector. Private building barely moved: +0.7%.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>CDMX WILL REBUILD THE FIDEL CASTRO AND CHE GUEVARA SCULPTURES REMOVED ILLEGALLY</u>

Mexico City's government announced the official restoration of the life-size sculptures of Fidel Castro and Che Guevara — the "Encuentro" set — one year after the Cuauhtémoc borough administration removed them without institutional authorization. The city's Culture Secretariat will reproduce the original design for a new public site.

"They will be placed in another location so we no longer have problems of this kind," said Mayor Clara Brugada.

The piece marked the spot in Tabacalera where Fidel and Che first met in 1955 — the meeting from which the Granma expedition was born.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>POISONED COMMUNITIES NETWORK DEMANDS CANCELATION OF TOPOLOBAMPO PETROCHEMICAL COMPLEX</u>

Renacer, a national network of Mexican communities poisoned by industry, demanded the federal government definitively cancel the petrochemical corridor planned for Ohuira Bay, Sinaloa: Proman's GPO ammonia plant, the Mexinol methanol plant, gas pipelines and port infrastructure.

The bay is a Ramsar-protected wetland of international importance — and the livelihood of thousands of fishing families. Swiss-German capital against a Mexican wetland.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>US OPENS DOOR TO REVIEWING MEXICO'S PENDING EXTRADITION REQUESTS</u>

Acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche said Mexico's unanswered extradition petitions "should be reviewed, of course" — while admitting he had no details. Between 2018 and 2026, Mexico filed 269 extradition requests with Washington; 233 remain pending, including former Tamaulipas governor García Cabeza de Vaca, wanted for organized crime and money laundering.

Sheinbaum has asked for reciprocity: in eight years, not one of those 269 requests has been completed.

Trump's deputy chief of staff for policy claimed Mexican cartels "control the territory," and that is why "the judicial, political and legal systems" of Mexico do not function — putting the cartels "in exactly the same legal situation as ISIS or Al Qaeda," except they operate "a few meters" from the US border instead of thousands of miles away.
